key_insight: The paper introduces structured quantum circuits that are both complexity-hard to simulate and encodable in a quantum code, enabling high-fidelity sampling with built-in verification.
engineering_relevance: It offers a practical path toward scalable, error-detected quantum sampling experiments by reducing effective gate errors and certifying output fidelity from circuit structure and syndrome measurements.
method: Design structured circuits with provable sampling hardness.
Encode the computation in spacetime quantum codes to suppress errors.
Use code-syndrome post-selection to certify a device-dependent fidelity bound.
evidence_signal: In a 70-qubit, depth-70 Clifford circuit doped with 468 T gates, the authors used 97 physical qubits, achieved about 10× error suppression after syndrome post-selection, and reported a fidelity lower bound of 0.284 at 95% confidence.
watch_item: The fidelity certificate is device dependent and still relies on noise assumptions, so deployment will require careful validation on specific hardware.
paper_title: Sampling hard circuits with verifiably high fidelity
